source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Austin campus publishes 19 MW of IT capacity across 242,000 square feet, and that is the only power figure the operator discloses.

The disclosure stops there. The spec page does not divide the 19 MW between the two buildings, does not give a power density per rack, and does not name a tenant. Any rack count derived from it depends on an assumed density, not on a published one. The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and TIA-942, describe what the campus is permitted to host, not who occupies it.

For AI specifically, the useful fact is the size of the published number and the silence around it. Nineteen megawatts is a real quantity of IT load, and IT load is the input that training and inference draw on. But capacity is not consumption, and a campus can hold a certification and a megawatt figure for years without that load being used for AI at all. Nothing here connects the 19 MW to a workload.

Within Texas, this campus ranks tenth among the 19 facilities in the state that publish a megawatt figure, against a published state total of 475.41 MW, or about 4 percent. Texas has 137 mapped facilities, so the 19 with numbers are a self-selected slice. That share measures disclosure, not the grid, and the grid is not described in this data.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
